title: One Ångström at the Selenocysteine Shield — Schoenheimer Heavy-Water Lipid Turnover, Ursini PHGPx & Stockwell Ferroptosis to 1.01 Å Wild-Type Human GPX4 Sec46 (PDB 6HN3) & Erastin-Locked System xc- (PDB 7EPZ)

teenKit.tldr: Your cells use a specialized selenium-powered shield to prevent a catastrophic, iron-driven chain reaction of cell death called ferroptosis. By looking at atomic-level protein structures, scientists can finally see exactly how this molecular armor operates and what happens when it breaks.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how cells control this destructive lipid fire opens up revolutionary ways to treat stubborn cancers, stroke damage, and rare genetic bone disorders.
keyTakeaways: Ferroptosis is a newly defined form of programmed cell death driven by uncontrolled oxidation of cell membrane fats in the presence of iron.
GPX4 is a vital antioxidant enzyme that uses a rare amino acid called selenocysteine to neutralize lipid peroxides and keep cell membranes safe.
Advanced molecular imaging (like X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM) lets scientists view these life-or-death protein mechanisms down to a single Ångström.

vocab.meaning: The 21st amino acid, featuring a reactive selenium atom that allows key enzymes to swiftly neutralize toxic cell-damaging peroxides.
A distinct type of cell death caused by an unstoppable wave of iron-catalyzed rust destroying the fats in cell membranes.
An ultra-tiny unit of measurement equal to one-tenth of a nanometre, used by scientists to map individual atoms within proteins.
A chemical compound that jams the cell's nutrient import machinery, locking the gate and triggering ferroptosis.

quiz.question: What is the primary driver of ferroptosis in cell membranes?
options: Excessive accumulation of water molecules inside the nucleus
Rapid breakdown of cellular DNA by viral infections
Complete depletion of cellular glucose stores
quiz.explanation: Ferroptosis is specifically defined by the iron-catalyzed, destructive oxidation of lipids within cell membranes.

quiz.question: What rare element makes the GPX4 enzyme uniquely powerful at stopping cellular damage?
quiz.explanation: GPX4 utilizes selenocysteine, incorporating a reactive selenium atom to quickly neutralize dangerous lipid peroxides.

quiz.question: What does PDB 7EPZ capture about the human xCT-4F2hc protein?
options: It shows the protein binding to water during heavy-water lipid turnover.
It displays the mutation responsible for Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
It reveals the antiporter locked in an inward-open state by the drug erastin.
It measures the exact temperature at which cells undergo thermal lysis.
quiz.explanation: PDB 7EPZ is a cryo-EM structure showing the human xCT antiporter jammed and locked in an inward-open state by erastin.
